definition: Visual capture is the recording of visual scenes, here in panoramic form, so they can be used to study how features of an environment shape human perception and emotion. In this source, it is part of a framework for examining emotional changes across a continuous landscape.

reasons: The packet supports that panoramic visual capture is one component of an integrated framework, but it does not define visual capture itself as the recording of visual scenes or state that this recording is specifically used to study how landscape features shape human perception and emotion.
The broader explanatory clause about studying environmental features and human emotion goes beyond the packet’s wording and is not directly supported as a definition of the term.

The definition states that “Visual capture is the recording of visual scenes,” but the packet only describes “panoramic visual capture” as part of an integrated framework and does not explicitly define it as “recording of visual scenes.”

The definition’s framing as “part of a framework for examining emotional changes across a continuous landscape” is broadly supported (linear landscapes; emotional fluctuations), but the additional explanatory phrasing about “features of an environment shape human perception and emotion” is only partially supported and not tied directly to what “visual capture” specifically is.
